section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section presents findings from a large-scale data collection on creative achievement, noting a self-selection bias among participants who completed the optional CAQ, showing higher education, cognitive ability, and interest in ideas. The study found a clear linear relationship between cognitive ability (ICAR60 scores) and total creative achievement (CAQ scores), with no evidence for a threshold hypothesis. It also explored the relationship between age and creative achievement, finding that the association became more positive when removing easily endorsed items, suggesting different achievement patterns across age groups. The data further indicated marked variability in predictive strength for creative achievement across different psychological domains, with vocational interests being more predictive than Big Five traits and cognitive ability in every domain.

It highlights a self-selection bias among participants who responded to the CAQ, showing they had higher education, cognitive ability (ICAR60 scores), and interest in ideas. The data also revealed that vocational interests were generally more predictive of creative achievement across various domains than Big Five traits and cognitive ability.
